physical_limits: Surface pressure: Earth about 1013 hPa, Mars about 6 hPa (CO₂).
Mars has no global magnetic field and a thin atmosphere, so surface radiation is far higher.
Present-day Mars is not the ancient Jezero lake; today's surface records the result of those processes.

formulas.scalar_distance: d_k = |x_E,k - x_P,k|   (same units on both bodies)
formulas.distribution_distance: d_k = W1(F_E,k, F_P,k) = integral_0^1 |F_E,k^-1(u) - F_P,k^-1(u)| du   (equal-area cells, 500 midpoint quantiles)
formulas.family_score: S_g = sum_k a_k|g * s_k   (nonredundant features; a_k|g sum to 1; every required feature must be eligible)
formulas.observed_index: 100 * sum_g w_g I_g S_g / sum_g w_g I_g   (undefined when no family qualifies)
formulas.evidence_coverage: sum_g w_g I_g   (share of the planned profile weight that is measured and comparable)

parameters.d_k: Distance between the Earth and planetary measurement of feature k, in the feature's own units (degrees or metres).
parameters.tau_k: Material-difference tolerance in the same units: the median W1 between unselected pairs of Earth land windows (Earth terrain contrast), accepted only if it is at least 3 times the resolution floor.
parameters.delta_k: Resolution floor: what moving the reference 2 km and changing the DEM product alone produce. Differences at or below it cannot separate sites.
parameters.a_k|g: Weight of feature k inside family g (equal across nonredundant scored features).
parameters.w_g: Planned weight of family g in the task profile. Provisional preferences from analog-evidence-v2, awaiting independent scientific review.
parameters.I_g: 1 when family g passes its comparability and quality rules for both AOIs, otherwise 0 with a recorded reason.

validation_status: Experimental. Tolerances come from Earth terrain contrast and measured resolution limits; the method has not been tested against expert-labelled analogues, negative controls chosen by experts or field outcomes.
notice: Indices are project-defined bounded indices on the stated measurements. They are not probabilities, confidence levels, percentages of identity, NASA standards or mission-suitability ratings.

population.caveat: The background windows come from tiles first downloaded for candidate sites: arid and mountainous regions are over-represented, and windows inside one region are spatially correlated. 4 regions, not 88 independent samples.

discrimination.notice: Discrimination analysis. Ranges and shares describe tested scenarios and an unselected background sample; they are not confidence intervals.
discrimination.interpretation: At a 60 m grid the index separates low-relief from rugged terrain well, but many unselected low-relief Earth windows also score highly. Read a candidate's background share (the fraction of unselected windows that score at least as high) before reading its index.
